Tappuah
TAP-poo-ah
proper noun
Hebrew Tappuach, “apple” or “apple place,” the name of towns on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh and in the lowland of Judah.

See also: Tappuah

📖 Biblical Definition

Tappuah, the “apple town,” marks a border. On the great line between the sons of Joseph it stood: “The border went out from Tappuah westward unto the river Kanah” (Jos 16:8), and the boundary between the two tribes ran through its very fields: “Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim” (Jos 17:8). Its Canaanite king had already fallen before Joshua: “The king of Tappuah, one” (Jos 12:17). Another Tappuah lay in the lowland of Judah: “And Zanoah, and Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam” (Jos 15:34). The careful drawing of these lines is not tedious record but covenant faithfulness: the LORD who promised the land to Abraham measured it out tribe by tribe and field by field, so that every family had its portion by lot from His hand. Tappuah on the seam between Ephraim and Manasseh testifies that God is a God of order, not confusion, and that the inheritance of His people is no vague hope but a surveyed and given possession. The lines are fallen unto His saints in pleasant places; their heritage is sure because He apportions it.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A border town between Ephraim and Manasseh (Jos 16:8; 17:8), with another in the lowland of Judah (Jos 15:34); a witness to the exact, covenanted apportioning of the inheritance.

expand to see more

TAPPUAH, “apple place,” a town on the Ephraim-Manasseh border, and another in the Judean lowland.

Its Canaanite king was smitten by Joshua (Jos 12:17).

The tribal boundary ran through its land (Jos 16:8; 17:8).

A second Tappuah is numbered among the lowland cities of Judah (Jos 15:34).

A witness to the ordered, lot-given apportioning of Israel’s inheritance.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 16:8 — "The border went out from Tappuah westward unto the river Kanah; and the goings out thereof were at the sea."

Jos 17:8 — "Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim;"

Jos 12:17 — "The king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;"

Jos 15:34 — "And Zanoah, and Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam,"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A border town of the apple; the entry recovers that God apportions His people’s inheritance by exact and faithful measure, not by chance.

expand to see more

Tappuah stirs no modern controversy, but the boundary it marks rebukes the assumption that the land-lists of Joshua are dry and dispensable record. Every measured line is the LORD keeping His oath to Abraham, dividing the promise field by field so that no tribe was forgotten and no family left without a portion.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God is a God of order, and that the inheritance of His people rests upon His faithful apportioning. The lines are fallen unto the saints in pleasant places (Psa 16:6). What looks like tedious geography is the surveyor’s proof of a covenant kept. So too the believer’s eternal inheritance is not a vague hope but a portion measured, sealed, and reserved by the hand of God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Tappuach, “apple,” a border town of Ephraim and Manasseh and a town of the Judean lowland.

expand to see more

Tappuah — Hebrew Tappuach, “apple” or “apple place.”

A town on the boundary of Ephraim and Manasseh.

Its king was among the thirty-one smitten by Joshua (Jos 12:17).

A second Tappuah lay in the lowland (shephelah) of Judah (Jos 15:34).

A marker of the exact, covenanted division of the inheritance.

Usage

"The border of Joseph ran from Tappuah westward to the river Kanah."

"Manasseh held the land of Tappuah, but the town fell to Ephraim."

"Tappuah preaches that God measures His people’s inheritance by faithful lot."
